review_notes: I read the whole file and the other uses of pageKernelExclusion (PageKernelPopulation.lean and the grep hits elsewhere). The other files treat it as an opaque set and only use the two theorems here. The only simp-interface problem I found is that the definition has no equation lemmas. Each of the three proofs unfolds the definition itself with simp only and then rebuilds the case-specific rewrites. I did not run Lean. I did not check the exact shape of the generated match equation lemmas, so the proposed lemmas are unverified. I did not recommend making these lemmas @[simp] globally, since the conditional large-case lemma is better applied by name.

findings.declaration: pageKernelExclusion (definition) and its uses in page_kernel_retention / page_kernel_exclusion_count
findings.excerpt:
match selectedPageZero P Q with
  | none => ∅
  | some e => if R < (e.modulus : ℝ) then largeConductorKernelCandidates e.modulus else ∅
findings.problem: The definition has no equation lemmas for its three cases (no selected zero, large modulus, small modulus). Each consumer instead unfolds it with `simp only [pageKernelExclusion, he, ite_eq_left hlarge]`, and each repeats the case-specific `ite_eq_left` or `ite_eq_right` rewrite, with `Finset.notMem_empty`, `Finset.filter_false`, `Finset.card_empty` and `Nat.cast_zero` added in the empty cases. This happens at lines 33, 44, 48 and 49. The unfold-then-ite pattern is duplicated, and any later consumer must reproduce it. Unfolding the definition also exposes the `match` and `ite` internals in the simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Add three small equation lemmas next to the definition. Each can be proved by `simp [pageKernelExclusion, he]`, with `ite_eq_left` or `ite_eq_right` for the conditional cases. (1) `pageKernelExclusion_of_none (h : selectedPageZero P Q = none) : pageKernelExclusion P Q R = ∅`, marked @[simp]. (2) `pageKernelExclusion_of_some_of_lt (he : selectedPageZero P Q = some e) (h : R < (e.modulus : ℝ)) : pageKernelExclusion P Q R = largeConductorKernelCandidates e.modulus`. (3) `pageKernelExclusion_of_some_of_le (he : selectedPageZero P Q = some e) (h : ¬ R < (e.modulus : ℝ)) : pageKernelExclusion P Q R = ∅`. Keep (2) and (3) as plain conditional rewrite lemmas, or @[simp] if wanted, since their hypotheses are discharged from local facts. Then `heq` becomes `pageKernelExclusion_of_some_of_lt he hlarge`. The case split in page_kernel_exclusion_count becomes `simp [pageKernelExclusion_of_some_of_le he hlarge, hE]`, without repeating the `Finset.filter_false` and `card_empty` chain.
findings.benefit: Callers rewrite by named lemmas and never unfold the match/ite. The three case analyses are stated once and the proofs are shorter and less brittle. Future lemmas about the exclusion set, such as monotonicity in R or membership characterisations, can reuse them.
